written: 2026-10-12, before any H2 frame is rendered, any model exists or any training job runs
author_directions: 2026-10-11, verbatim: "You are doing all of the judgement work through trial and error." and "our goal is to spend as little money as possible." 2026-10-12, verbatim: "Ideally, we ship without any dependencies, and build our own infrastructure in R&D, to minimize reliance on outside sources."
why: The original data rules were written without a cost estimate. RT's GPU path tracer renders about 1e8 samples a second on the RTX 4090 (1280 x 720 at 1024 spp in 9.4 s, RT PROGRESS step 9). A 1920 x 1080 target at 4,096 spp is about 85 s; the per-pixel rule (standard error under 1% of the mean on 99% of pixels) needs a per-sample coefficient of variation under 0.64 at 4,096 spp, which indirect light in the interiors does not reach, so the rule would demand 1e4 to 1e5 spp a frame. Training is local and short (no cloud), so the data is scaled to what one RTX session can render. Nothing here touches a success bound, a control or the split's test scenes.

changes.resolution: denoise mode only, input and output 480 x 270. The 2x upscale mode is deferred: not built, not trained, reported as not done.
changes.targets: test and validation frames 8,192 spp; training frames 4,096 spp; the input's sample (index 0) is never among the target's samples (indices 1 and up, same counter-based seed), so input and target noise are independent. The original per-pixel rule is computed and reported for every frame but does not drop frames. In its place a validity check runs at evaluation: on every test frame the target's noise (mean over pixels of the variance of the mean, linear luminance) must be below 10% of the smallest method MSE against that target; a frame that fails it is reported and excluded from every method alike.
changes.camera_paths: test and validation: one path of 64 frames a scene. Training: paths of 32 frames.
changes.split_additions: train gains RT's dense_block (allowed: additions to train). The HW hall is used in its H1.1b form without coincident faces (evidence/hw-h1-1b-bounds.json), the same scene minus hidden faces. Training uses retro_room, dense_block, terrain seeds 0 and 1, debris seeds 0 and 1, and the built-in test scene; the other listed training scenes and seeds are not rendered in this pass (nothing moves between splits).
changes.ghosting: M3's metric needs a moving mesh and its coverage; the path tracer's sequences move only the camera. Ghosting here keeps M3's form, mean |output - reference| over the trail pixels, with the trail defined by camera disocclusion: pixels whose first-hit triangle differs from the triangle at their reprojected position in the previous frame, or whose reprojection leaves the frame, accumulated over the previous 8 frames as in M3. This is an adaptation and is labelled so.
changes.taa_baseline: M3's taa::resolve (raw/renderer/taa.hpp, read only, called unchanged) run on SVGF's output with the path tracer's motion and an expected previous depth computed from depth and the two cameras
changes.flip_status: still unchecked against the BSD-3 reference test pair (that needs a download the author has not approved); every FLIP number is labelled unchecked, and the verdict rule for FLIP stands as written with that label

unchanged: success bounds (FLIP, PSNR, temporal instability, ghosting by the interval rules), the 2.0 ms budget at 1920 x 1080 on the RTX 4090 through cooperative matrix, inference parity within 1e-2, every control that must fail, the leakage hash check, training jobs of at most 60 minutes checkpointed every 10, hyperparameters chosen on validation only, and test scenes iso_street, raw-hall and raw-hero
does_not_prove: Anything at 1920 x 1080 beyond the inference budget; anything about the 2x upscale mode.
